he bulk properties of gases, liquids, and solids—molar volume, density, com­ pressibility, and thermal expansion, among others—differ widely, often by orders of magnitude. All of these properties depend on the temperature and pres­ sure. The local structure—the arrangement of atoms or molecules on the nanome­ ter length scale—is the key microscopic feature that distinguishes the three states of matter from one another and explains the differences in their bulk properties. The average separation between molecules, and the nature of the intermolecular forces, determine the local structure and therefore the properties of the bulk.
